articles.title: INDIA–NEPAL JOINT MILITARY EXERCISE ‘SURYAKIRAN XX’ COMMENCES IN NEPAL
articles.description: New Delhi. Asal Baat news. The 20th edition of the India–Nepal Joint Military Exercise SURYAKIRAN commenced today at the Nepal Army Battle School, Saljhandi, Nepal. The exercise is scheduled to be conducted from 25 November to 08 December 2026. The Opening Ceremony was graced by Major General Purna Bahadur Khatri, General Officer Commanding, Mid Western Division, Nepal Army. The Indian Army contingent, comprising 334 personnel, is being represented by troops from the KUMAON Regiment. The Nepal Army contingent, comprising an equal number of personnel, is being represented by troops from Shri Jawla Dal Battalion. The aim of the exercise is to enhance interoperability, operational coordination and mutual understanding between the two Armies through joint training in counter-insurgency and counter-terrorism operations in challenging terrain. The scope of the exercise includes joint tactical operations, heliborne operations, disaster response and medical training. Troops from both Armies will exchange operational experiences and best practices while refining tactics, techniques and procedures to enhance joint operational effectiveness. Exercise SURYAKIRAN is an annual bilateral military exercise conducted alternately in India and Nepal. The exercise will further strengthen bilateral defence cooperation, foster mutual trust and camaraderie between the two Armies and reaffirm the shared commitment of both nations towards regional peace, stability and security.
